title: AuditLogViewer
wrapsNative: MonarchListRow rows in MonarchCursorList, MonarchBottomSheet for one event, android.text.format.DateUtils for relative and absolute times; MonarchSearchBar and MonarchTag (the filter-bar recipe), MonarchAvatar, MonarchBadge, MonarchDescriptionList with copy, MonarchDownloadReportButton for the CSV export
summary: A recipe, not a component: a searchable, filterable audit log of who did what, when and from where, as list rows that open one event's details (including field changes) in a bottom sheet.
whenToUse: For workspace security and admin screens where people review sign-ins, permission changes, exports and API activity.
whenNotToUse: For one request's raw details use the log-drawer recipe; for streaming output use MonarchLogViewer; for a person's own activity feed use a timeline.
api: MonarchSearchBar(query = query, onQueryChange = …, onSearch = …, placeholder = "Search the audit log")
MonarchTag(text = "Automations and API", selected = …, onSelectedChange = …); MonarchDownloadReportButton(onDownload = …, labels = MonarchDownloadReportButtonLabels(label = "Export CSV"))

MonarchCursorList(items = events, label = "Audit log", hasMore = …, onLoadMore = …, key = { it.id }) { event -> ListItem(headlineContent = …, overlineContent = { MonarchBadge(kind) }, supportingContent = …, leadingContent = { MonarchAvatar(…, decorative = true) }, trailingContent = { Text(relative time) }, modifier = Modifier.clickable(onClickLabel = "Details") { … }) }
ModalBottomSheet(onDismissRequest = …) { Column(Modifier.verticalScroll(…)) { MonarchText("Event details", heading = true); MonarchDescriptionList(items = …); MonarchButton("Close", …) } }

options.name: events
options.description: Each event: id, time in epoch milliseconds, actor (name, kind), action, target, IP, device, location, source, reason, field changes.

options.name: query and filters
options.description: The search text and filter tags; the app filters, or queries the server and pages with the cursor.

options.name: export
options.description: Export CSV of the filtered events.

options.name: now
options.description: The instant relative times are measured from.

states.name: events
states.description: One row per event: overline tag for automations and API keys, actor and action, target, relative time.

states.name: loading / more
states.description: MonarchCursorList shows placeholders on the first load and a load-more footer after.

states.name: empty
states.description: MonarchCursorList's empty state; for a search, say no events match.

states.name: error
states.description: MonarchCursorList's failed state with Try again.

states.name: details
states.description: A bottom sheet titled Event details with time, actor, action, target, IP address with copy, device and the field changes as before → after.

appearance: Material 3 list items on the surface with Monarch avatars and badges, the search bar and tags above, and a bottom sheet of description lists for one event. Light, dark and both high-contrast themes follow from those components.
platformNotes: The web ships AuditLogViewer as a pattern with a table (time, actor, action, target, IP and device columns), a details drawer from the side with a before-and-after table, an export button and messages. On a phone, as on iOS, it is a recipe: the table becomes list rows that open a bottom sheet, the before-and-after table becomes description items reading Before → After, and the relative time with a tooltip becomes DateUtils' relative text with the full time in the sheet. Paging uses MonarchCursorList.
accessibility: Each row is one element whose click is labelled Details; the avatar is decorative and the actor is text.
Automation and API actors carry a word badge, not only a color or an icon.
The sheet is modal, its title has heading semantics, and Back closes it.
The IP address has a copy button named for it.
The search bar and tags keep their own roles and selected states.
edgeCases: An unknown actor: show "Unknown" instead of an empty name.
A field set for the first time or cleared: write None for the missing side.
Long targets wrap in the row; the full text is in the sheet.
Keep the event's id in rememberSaveable so the open sheet survives rotation.

examples.title: Workspace audit log
examples.setupTemplate:
data class AuditEvent(
    val id: String,
    val time: Long,
    val actor: String,
    val kind: String?,
    val action: String,
    val target: String?,
    val source: String?,
    val area: String = "members",
)
val events = listOf(
    AuditEvent({{events.0.id}}, {{events.0.time|millis}}, {{events.0.actor}}, null, {{events.0.action}}, {{events.0.target}}, null),
    AuditEvent({{events.1.id}}, {{events.1.time|millis}}, {{events.1.actor}}, null, {{events.1.action}}, null, null, "security"),
    AuditEvent({{events.2.id}}, {{events.2.time|millis}}, {{events.2.actor}}, {{events.2.kind}}, {{events.2.action}}, {{events.2.target}}, {{events.2.source}}, "settings"),
    AuditEvent({{events.3.id}}, {{events.3.time|millis}}, {{events.3.actor}}, {{events.3.kind}}, {{events.3.action}}, {{events.3.target}}, null),
)
// The kind as a label: "automation" is Automation, "api" is API.
fun kindLabel(kind: String) = if (kind == "api") "API" else kind.replaceFirstChar { it.uppercase() }
val timeFormat = DateTimeFormatter.ofLocalizedDateTime(FormatStyle.MEDIUM)
    .withLocale(Locale.forLanguageTag({{locale}}))
    .withZone(ZoneId.of({{timeZone}}))
var area by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf("all") }
var openId by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf<String?>(null) }
val shown = events.filter { area == "all" || it.area == area }

fun kindLabel(kind: String) = if (kind == "api") "API" else kind.replaceFirstChar { it.uppercase() }
